declienting: Ported the Handlebars template to a React component: the {{#if}} guards became conditional JSX, and {{{description}}} (raw HTML interpolation) became a description: ReactNode prop the caller composes.

Replaced the BEM classes (heading-with-description__eyebrow/__heading/__description and the --left/--center modifiers) with Tailwind utilities; the alignment modifier became an alignment: 'left' | 'center' prop toggling items-* / text-*.
Dropped the .rtf .rtf--inherit-type rich-text container on the description; it now takes composed content and styles only inline links (color-link), leaving prose rendering to the caller.

Mapped tokens onto the library semantic layer: heading to color-text-primary; eyebrow and description to color-text-secondary; the 24px eyebrow-to-heading gap to spacing-m; the 32px heading-to-description gap to spacing-l.
Dropped client sample copy (the 'Our Handprint' eyebrow and the climate-change heading and body text) — every string is a prop.

Kept verbatim: the

-heading /

-eyebrow semantics, group-level alignment, and collapse-when-empty for both optional parts — the accessibility contract that made it worth capturing.
